newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn rallies to five-month highs on funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn rallies to five-month highs on funds.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher with most contracts up roughly one-half the daily trading limit amid fresh five-month highs, traders said.

Fund buying, estimated at at least 20 million bushels, a surge in soybeans and bullish input from Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitment of Traders report triggered the advances, sources said.

"We have the port strike hanging over our heads, the commitments were a little friendly and it's a little wet in northern Brazil but that's mostly in the coffee and corn areas," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Corn contracts traded in fast dealings early as the market was buffeted by the soaring soybean market.
Soybeans gained on concerns about an upcoming port strike in Brazil and on talk about rain-delayed harvesting of the Brazilian soybean crop, traders said.
A union official Monday said workers at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua will start a 24-hour strike on Wednesday and there was concern the strike could spread to other ports.
Corn closed three to 6-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up six at $3.02-3/4.

Nearby March broke above the $3.00 resistance area and touched a session high of $3.03 per bushel, the highest level for that month since $3.00-1/2 was reached on October 10. The contract high for March is $3.94-1/2 set on July 12.
There was follow-through buying from the overnight trend.
Fund buying boosted corn in CBOT's Project A overnight session and traders agreed the surging soybean market kept intact the strong tone in corn futures going into Monday's open outcry session.
Soy also rallied to new five-month highs on fund buying with the South American concerns plus lingering talk of forecasts for low ending stocks of U.S. soy and slow farmer selling mentioned.
Also cited was bullish input from a CFTC report, the traders said.
"The commitments were on the lighter side of what was expected," a trader said.

Traders said Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report showed as of February 25, funds were long corn by roughly 367.1 million bushels and short by 120.3 million bushels, or a net long position of about 247 million bushels.
The market was expecting the net long position of funds to range from 250 million to 300 million bushels.
The posting Monday of no deliveries on March futures surprised no one. No deliveries are expected to surface on the March contract, floor sources said.
USDA's weekly export inspections report showed the corn tally for the week ended February 27 at 31.41 million bushels, below the range of trade estimates from 34.0 million to 37.0 million bushels.

Merrill Lynch Futures bought five million bushels each of May and July, traders said. Refco Inc bought three million each of May and July and ADM Investor Services sold four million May, they said. Smith Barney sold 13.0 million bushels of May, traders said.
Technicians early Monday cited first resistance in the March at $3.00-1/2 and second resistance at $3.11. The session high for March was $3.03.
First support in the March was $2.90 and second support was at $2.79-1/2. The session low was $2.99-1/2.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed at 86-1/2 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 80,414 traded Friday.

In corn options, Refco Inc sold 1,000 July $3.10 calls at 13 to 13-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 500 May $2.80 calls at 23 to 24 cents and LFG Futures sold 500 July $3.60 calls at 4-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, above the 16,473 traded Friday.
